_doc: A T8 trapezoidal lead screw, 8 mm outside, 2 mm thread pitch, the unbranded hobby part: community until measured. The main figures are the common 4-start, 8 mm lead (Tr8x8(P2)); variants lead-2 and lead-4 are the 1-start and 2-start screws on the same thread form. DIN 103 / ISO 2904 tabulates Tr8 only at 1.5 mm pitch, so the 2 mm thread is not a tabulated size: its dimensions come from the standard's formulas. Efficiency and self-locking are estimates at a friction nobody publishes for brass or POM on these screws: measure it before trusting a screw to hold a load unpowered.
name: t8-screw

lead-2.source: Wenzel Lab T8 lead screw nut, https://wenzel-lab.github.io/syringe-pumps-and-controller/parts/mech/lead-screw-nut.html

lead-4.source: Rat Rig POM lead screw nut, TR8*4, https://ratrig.com/leadscrew-nut-pom-tr8-4.html

thread.rule: Trapezoidal, 8 mm outside, 8 mm lead, 2 mm pitch, four starts
thread.source: Pololu traveling nut for TR8x8(P2) rods, https://pololu.com/product/2688/specs

diameter.source: Handson Technology T8 flange nut data sheet, https://handsontec.com/dataspecs/linear%20motion/T8-Copper-Nut.pdf

pitch.rule: Thread pitch, flank to flank of the next start
pitch.source: Handson Technology T8 flange nut data sheet, https://handsontec.com/dataspecs/linear%20motion/T8-Copper-Nut.pdf

lead.rule: Travel in one turn: pitch times starts
lead.source: Handson Technology T8 flange nut data sheet, https://handsontec.com/dataspecs/linear%20motion/T8-Copper-Nut.pdf

starts.source: Handson Technology T8 flange nut data sheet, https://handsontec.com/dataspecs/linear%20motion/T8-Copper-Nut.pdf

pitch_diameter.rule: Pitch diameter, from the ISO 2904 formula d2 = d - 0.5 P (Tr8 at 2 mm pitch is not in its table)
pitch_diameter.source: Roymech trapezoidal threads (ISO 2904 table and formulas), https://roymech.org/Useful_Tables/Screws/Trapezoidal.html

root_diameter.rule: Root diameter d3 = d - 2 (0.5 P + ac), ISO 2904 formula, with ac = 0.25 mm taken from the table's 9 mm x 2 mm row (D4 = 9.5). That table has typos elsewhere: measure it
root_diameter.source: Roymech trapezoidal threads (ISO 2904 table and formulas), https://roymech.org/Useful_Tables/Screws/Trapezoidal.html

helix_angle.rule: Lead angle at the pitch diameter, atan(lead / (pi * pitch_diameter))
helix_angle.source: Roymech trapezoidal threads (ISO 2904 table and formulas), https://roymech.org/Useful_Tables/Screws/Trapezoidal.html

friction_coefficient.rule: An assumed thread friction: igus's published figure for iglidur J running dry. No figure was found for brass or POM on these screws
friction_coefficient.source: igus blog on lead screw efficiency, https://blog.igus.eu/?p=19485

efficiency_note.value: eta = tan(a) / tan(a + atan(f / cos 15 deg)), with a the helix angle. At f = 0.15: lead 8: helix 19.99 deg, about 66%, back-drives; lead 4: helix 10.31 deg, about 52%, back-drives; lead 2: helix 5.2 deg, about 36%, self-locks. Self-locking while tan(a) < f / cos 15 deg. igus finds dry single-start trapezoidal nuts run at 20 to 48%
efficiency_note.rule: Efficiency and back-driving, computed at the assumed friction. PBC Linear says efficiency is a calculated value and testing decides
efficiency_note.source: igus blog on lead screw efficiency, https://blog.igus.eu/?p=19485; PBC Linear, what is lead screw efficiency, https://pbclinear.com/blogs/blog/what-is-lead-screw-efficiency-in-linear-motion
